items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: Well yeah, that was during the recording with Clarence Riggins, I came to New York. I met Oliver in Chicago when I went from that same place just visiting with a friend of mine. But I never did no playing with him until I came to New York and was doing work with Clarence Riggins.

ctx.x: He goes way back too. I didn't think he was that old.

Yeah. He was only about two years younger than I. I was born in December. He was about three years old. Three years at the most. Did you get to hear Oliver play in those years? Yeah, I used to marry Oliver and Louis Armstrong because when they came up to San Luis, that's before I worked on them both days. They used to come, all of us come to San Luis, the fake miracle. And Louis Armstrong was with him. And after that they went Chicago. That's why I had Gerald Book, both there and Louis and Oliver together doing…
like that in all my life. It was so great. Well you played a lot with Oliver yourself later.

items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: I did the same thing with Joe Oliver, and all of them used to work for me.

ctx.x: Would you say your style was something like Oliver's?

Well some people say it. I don't know. I don't think so. But I hear on some records that they couldn't tell one from another. But I think it was different. I admire his style. But I thought it was different. But I heard several people say, you sound just like Joe Oliver. He made some records because I couldn't tell one from another. And I've made some records that were individuals by myself, one trumpet. And he made some with one trumpet, as they say with me on one record, and say to him on another. Which was the…
would say that you played with that played what you could call jazz? Well this band, I can say this ten piece band. That was about the first one.
